items.text: And now that's good placement, though they keep it to just one. Great yorker well outside off, he glides this out towards backward point
items.postText: Hope needs 11 more for a ton, though he probably he doesn't have an eye on that as much as a 250 here...
items.shortText: Nitish Kumar Reddy to Rutherford, 1 run

items.text: Quite full just outside off, he bunts this out towards long-off
items.shortText: Nitish Kumar Reddy to Hope, 1 run

items.text: Speared in quite full, right in the blockhole! Excellent bowling here. Batter can only glide this late, out towards backward point
items.shortText: Nitish Kumar Reddy to Rutherford, 1 run

items.preText: Shai Hope changing his bat in between overs.
items.text: Low full toss, he misses his lines and Hope doesn't miss on this awesome hit down the ground! Played under his eyes and he middles this just enough over mid-on
items.shortText: Nitish Kumar Reddy to Hope, SIX

items.text: He will get his century! Somehow it has burst through Tilak Varma's hands, who holds his hands up in despair, wondering how he did not pouch this. Was another full toss right on his waist, he shovels this across the line down to long-on, where really, he should have been caught at the ropes. But Tilak is in an awkward position and the ball flies over the ropes, it's a six. This is Hope's third T20I century, and West Indies finish on a mammoth 247 for 3.
items.postText: We have The Don in today's MATCHUP. Who can you connect him with? Shimron Hetmyer speaks to the broadcasters: "It's a pretty damn good score, to be honest. Little annoyed we didn't get to 250, but it's actually a really good score... In the first innings, there wasn't much grip with the slower balls. [On reverse bowling] I hope so, but looks like wicket is a tad bit drier." 9pm What an innings from West Indies. Sure, we've seen six-hitting aplenty in this series, but to see Hope operate at his best was truly something else. He's maybe having his best-ever white-ball series, including those boshing one-dayers earlier. Anyway, Hope had chased down 250 a few days ago. Today he brings WI up to 247 and sets the mandate for India: someone needs to repeat a Hope for India to have a shot at chasing this, as good as the conditions might be. We'll be back in fifteen minutes, when Abhimanyu will be here to take you through the first ten overs of the chase.
items.shortText: Nitish Kumar Reddy to Hope, SIX

items.preText:
9.01pm Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson bump fists before making their way to the middle. Samson on strike first up against Roston Chase. There is some delay because of a technical issue with the sightscreen.

Rose: "Only 3 people (Rohit, Babar, Shai) have 3 centuries in all 3 formats. Shai has 3 centuries in all 3 formats *in the last 15 months alone*! What a purple patch this is turning out to be!"

Mustafa Moudi : "Fun Fact: This is the 3rd Instance of a Captain scoring exactly 102 Not Out this Series. Only the 3rd T20I didnt have sny of Hope snd Shreyas scoring this score !!" 8.58pm Hello again, folks. Should be a challenging chase, this. As we wait, here are some stats, courtesy Sampath.

Shai Hope - first West Indies batter with three hundreds in men's T20Is. 5th player from a full member with multiple hundreds in a series. Salt, Samson, Tilak and Sahibzada Farhan are the others.

Tenth score of 240 or more in T20s at Hyderabad, the joint-most at a venue, alongside Wankhede.
items.text: Samson gets India's chase started with a boundary! Too short outside off from Chase and Samson is able to clear his front leg and flat-bat it back over the bowler's head. Hit too hard for long-on to come across
On a length just outside off, punched down to mid-off
On a length outside off again, Samson tries to flat-bat it past mid-off but hits it off the bottom edge. Mid-off easily stops it
Length ball outside off spins in from outside off, Samson nudges it to backward square leg for a single
On a length outside leg, Abhishek nudges it to mid-on's left for a single to get off the mark
Flat and very full outside off, Samson just eases it into the vacant midwicket region for a single

items.preText:
Shamar Joseph from the other end

Azweer : "For West Indies, In this series, Chase is for bowling, what Hope is for batting. "
items.text: Length ball angled into him from outside off, Samson nudges it to midwicket

Beaten by the pace! Nearly 149kph, length ball pitching on off and angled across, Samson looks to make room and swing it away leg-side, but the ball goes between the inside edge and his pads, and over the stumps
Back of length delivery rocketing into Samson, who sways back and opens the face to glide it to short third. And wait, Shamar has overstepped!

Not what Samson wanted to do, but the result is close to what he would have wanted. Short ball on off, 145kph, and Samso looks to hook it away. Looks like it went off the shoulder over Hope and for four. Given runs off the bat. Maybe an inside edge onto his shoulder?
Boshed away! Full ball sits up nicely as Samson picks it early and whips it away over cow corner
Samson in the mood! 149kph, but it's in the slot just outside off, and Samson launches it down the ground and into the crowd! Just look at that backlift and follow-through!
Back-of-length delivery around off, Samson clips it out to deep midwicket

items.preText: Shadow-Shell: "@Azweer Wait, you brought up Chase and Hope in the same sentence but with not a single pun. Is that even legally allowed?"
items.text: Fires a full ball down leg. Keeper can only deflect it to short fine leg
Lovely stuff from Samson! This is fired in the blockhole outside off but Samson is able to play it with the open face to steer it past the diving point fielder for another boundary
Creamed over extra cover! Tossed up in the slot outside off and Samson plays a handsome lofted drive. And that's India's 2000th T20I six!
Samson will feel he's missed out there. This is dragged down on off and Samson pulls it away square of deep midwicket, but can't time it well enough to beat the fielder
Low full toss around leg, clipped out in front of square

items.preText: Chase changes angle. Around the wicket now
items.text: The ball's just flying off Samson's bat! This was all touch and timing! Too full around middle and Samson gently lofts it down the ground as he brings down his bat with the full face on display.
If the last one was all about timing, this was all power! Dragged short again by Chase and Samson swivels and pulls it away in front of square. Deep midwicket stood no chance this time!
